title: Where the records go
objective: Learners see how many member records from up to five source systems survive each stage of a customer data platform in a month (quality check, identity resolution, consent) and why the width of a flow, not the presence of an arrow, is what a capacity, licence or consent conversation should start from.

recommended.why: A Sankey makes volume the picture: the width of each band is the count, so the rejected, merged and consented shares are visible before anyone reads a number.

alternative.why: Plotly draws a Sankey from configuration; D3 with d3-sankey gives full control of labels, reveal order and what a narrow screen keeps. Which one would you put in a deck, and which in a course?

assumptions: Volumes, rejection rates and names are illustrative monthly figures for a fictional health plan; no real system or member is implied
Sources connect in the order member portal, claims system, contact centre, marketing platform, pharmacy; the control takes the first n
The quality check rejects a fixed share per source (invalid member numbers, missing dates of birth, test records); with the filter off every record passes
Identity resolution merges a record into an existing profile at the duplicate rate; merged records still update a member and are not lost
Every profile update reaches the service agent; only updates for members with marketing consent can also start a marketing journey
Flows are counts of records, rounded to whole records at each split, so every stage passes on exactly what it receives
units: rates: percent of the records entering a stage
playback: about 21 s, one scene per stage
checkDescription: Every stage passes on exactly what it receives, every record ends as rejected, marketing + service or service only, the filter switch removes every rejection when off, and the merged and consented shares match the sliders within rounding.
expectAtDefaults: m.totals.rejected > 0 && m.totals.rejected + m.totals.marketing + m.totals.service === m.totals.ingested && m.totals.merged > m.totals.rejected

learnerPrompts.predict: Set the duplicate rate to 60 % before you play. Does the number of records that can be marketed to go up, down or stay the same, and why?
learnerPrompts.explain: Turn the quality filter off. The marketing band gets wider. Explain to a product owner why that wider band is a problem, not a win.
